hypothesis: Under the explicitly assumed base-fee model, exact equal-net quantity across two discrete grids may require more capital/liquidity than allowed. A capped minimal covering spot purchase can leave unhedged long and unsellable dust which must remain owned inventory.
step_basis: Observed first-bar native trade quantity GCD only, not certified historical market-order filters. Do not import spot/perpetual/inverse rules as dated contract proof.
fee_basis: Same10bps base-asset spot-entry fee assumed by the old account; actual fee asset/rate/rounding unverified. No switch to BNB or quote fee to improve outcome.
caps: Use each original event's gross spot quantity and net short quantity as hard maximums. No larger cash/liquidity budget, retries, alternative fee/step grid or price selection.
method: Fraction/GCD coprime proof of minimum exact pair; floor max short lots under both caps, then ceil the smallest gross spot lots to cover. Retain net-minus-short and net-minus-sellable as distinct owned residuals. Cash/order filters are separate, unknown gates.
outputs: minimum exactly matched pair and whether it fits both original quantity caps
largest capped future lots and smallest covering spot lots; exact base-fee conservation
unhedged base inventory and exit-grid dust, no automatic conversion
entry notional thresholds above which the diagnostic orders would be rejected; actual minimum-notional values remain unknown
independent integer-unit reconstruction without importing factor implementation
stopping: Only arithmetic/constraint diagnosis, not a new financial return path or repaired quarter. Do not mark matched hedge or closed account when residual inventory survives.
